items._cn_summary: 法国高音萨克斯演奏家Émile Parisien携手钢琴手Yaron Herman、贝斯手Linda May Han Oh及印度塔布拉鼓手Prabhu Edouard，组成一支横跨东西方音乐语汇的四重奏。专辑以Gurdjieff与de Hartmann的冥想性作品开篇，将东欧神秘主义音阶与中东传统节奏并置，随后引入Anouar Brahem的《Badhra》展现精致内省的抒情对话。Parisien以跳跃的音程在高音区展开叙事，Herman的钢琴提供简约而清澈的和声框架，Edouard的塔布拉与声乐元素为整体注入流动的脉搏。原创曲目在巴洛克般的对位与爵士摇摆之间自由切换，既有中东色彩的《Bonbon》，也有Keith Jarrett式即兴段落，体现出对多元传统的开放态度。整体定位偏学院化、沉思型，强调文化融合的细腻质感而非激进实验。

items.body: Sébastien Guérive’s new Omega Point is a cinematic soundscape – something that resembles a soundtrack to a recently rediscovered sci-fi noir thriller. The album oscillates between moments of tranquility and pure suspense, balancing the two fairly well but always keeping the listener wanting a bit more. The album starts out with a track that builds – and it not only builds in suspense, tension and amplitude but it also lays the foundation for the rest of the album. What follows are tracks that embrace dualities – dark and light, ambient and upbeat, minimalist and detailed. Sébastien Guérive’s experience with acoustical instruments is apparent throughout the album – although Omega Point is comprised of mostly synthesizers it’s apparent that the timber and texture were obsessed over to achieve a color rich in harmonics. Although the album does have an 80s sound throughout, it never crosses that border being too processed or artificial, opting for the more natural and organic approach. The album will be available March 19 on vinyl & digital (Atypeek Music / The Orchard). Bellatrix ( single ) by Sébastien Guérive www.sebastienguerive.bandcamp.com
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑构建出类似科幻黑色电影配乐的声景，在宁静与悬疑之间反复切换。开篇曲目以渐进的张力、音量与质感铺陈整张专辑的基调，后续作品持续探索明暗、环境与节奏、极简与繁复的对立关系。尽管以合成器为主，但创作者对声学乐器的理解深入其中，使音色与质地呈现出丰富的泛音层次。整体带有八十年代复古质感，却刻意规避过度处理的人造痕迹，转向更自然有机的声音路径。专辑在氛围铺垫与悬念制造之间保持平衡，始终为听者保留进一步的期待空间。

items.body: As well as the well-deep, murky waters of bittersweet nostalgia and memory, ambient music is capable of stirring up emotions, too. Gazing into the water produces a true reflection of the self, be it good, bad, or indifferent. A single phrase can bring a whole host of memories back from the ether, echoing into the mind from another point in time, like a dozen ripples skirting over a silver lake. Means of Knowing is another beautiful album from Hotel Neon, who describe it as being ‘an exchange with the world, an effort to know it and ourselves more deeply’. Accompanying the still set is a flickering, short-circuiting socket of white noise. It’s a light drizzle upon the ambient texture: there’s no chance of a rain-out, and no deluge of distortion. Rain and melancholia are linked, but this exudes feelings of introspection and comfort. This is the sound of your favourite walk, taking place in woodland or over sands, gentle and yet striking, like an autumn breeze as it ruffles turning leaves and shakes high trees; a sudden whoosh that takes your breath away. The Earth has music for those who listen. The outsider may only pick up static, but you’ve taken this route a thousand times before, and you can hear its invisible music. You can hear the radio, and not the shrill buzz of static. You can hear life, and not death. Sure, the uneven path is the same, but it’s also different, changing with every passing day. The daisies grow along the sides of the bank, as do the bluebells, but the seasons change and sculpt the landscape, just as the seasons change the self. Nothing remains the same forever. We’re all constantly changing. A pair of feisty geese will try to blot out the encouraging sense of serenity, but the walk is beautiful, healing and restorative, rising higher than those angry honks, and music is a perfect companion. The years are condensed into this record. As a glint of sunlight will pour through a jade-painted leaf, so too does the subtle, shifting drone exhibit the same level of transparency, shining through in a beam of victory. The music is also its own being, capable of standing apart, of playing independently, of walking with you on this peaceable amble, and being a true friend. Music brightens everything at once, as would a burst of sunshine on a day of infinite cloud, but the music doesn’t become excitable. It’s introspective. It’s introverted. And there’s something buried within the music, kicking up and swirling around the music’s trainers like dirt and dried mud from a well-travelled path. Sounds from the physical world are inserted, deepening the connection, and processed synths run alongside them. When you cut through the bramble-like clutter in our own lives, you get to this. The soundtrack of your life (the original, uncut edition) is played in stereo, and the ambient runs through the narrow arteries and connecting veins. Similarly, it also runs through the leaves and their vein-like tunnels. Carrying life. Everything is connected. It runs deep. www.archivesdubmusic.bandcamp.com
items._cn_summary: Hotel Neon的《Means of Knowing》延续了深沉氛围音乐的脉络，以持续的合成器低鸣为主体，间或融入现实环境声采样，形成一种内省式的聆听体验。整张专辑如同一场穿越自然景观的漫步——林间落叶、岸边野花、偶发的鹅鸣都被织入绵密的音景之中，白噪声如细雨般轻轻覆盖在底层纹理上，却始终不破坏整体的宁静氛围。评论将音乐比作叶脉中的循环系统，强调其与自然世界的深层连接，合成器处理过的环境音与未处理的田野录音并行流动，模糊了人造与真实的边界。专辑不追求戏剧性的爆发，而是以细微的动态变化折射时间的流逝与自我的变迁，营造出一种既私密又开放的冥想空间，适合安静环境下的深度聆听。

items.body: If music unlocks the heart, then A Baleia (which means ‘The Whale’ in Portuguese) is a subtle rotating of the key, a 22-minute selection of soulful tape-recorded soundscapes. Will Samson’s latest album crafts kind, instrumental music, its soft, lulling tones originating from a state of deep relaxation and tranquil, limitless motion. Last summer, Samson spent some time in a flotation tank – a soundproofed pod where one floats in salted warm water while at the same time experiencing total darkness and weightlessness. This experience proved to be deeply healing and therapeutic, and these sensations ripple through the music, submerging it in a tide of sensuous strings and slow-moving atmospheres. Paradoxically, the music glows warmly as it lies in the dense depths of darkness. A feeling of unrestricted freedom is able to turn the locks of an ashen heart until it wakes up, changing its key, transcending into overwhelming euphoria. This is a utopic experience, but it’s a mere illusion, an imitation played out in the rigid confines of a cube, and that’s okay. That’s more than okay. You’re free, unattached to the world and its pressures, severed from its umbilical cord, a step out of reach from its outstretched, lingering hand. The music feels both detached and intimate, at once wrapped up in and removed from its surroundings. When the eyes open, they stare into the darkness. When the lids close, everything lights up. The music is in the world, but the pause button has been pushed, its license to pressurize and demand fully revoked. Soaking in the soothing texture is something close to bliss. The world continues to exist, and it continues to speak, but things are tuned out of range, like quiet voices coming from another room or a radio with its volume turned down. Senses are heightened. Featuring violin from Beatrijs De Klerck and Matt Resovich (of The Album Leaf), Samson also collaborates with Brumes and Benoit Pioulard, forming something of an ambient dream-team. The strings swell and meander, brushing against the gently-breathing body of music like eels slow-dancing in the deep. Under the water, everything’s unclothed, and strict regularity disappears. The music loosens, becomes elastic as it kisses the depths, with only a drum occasionally keeping up an appearance of perfect time, supporting and upholding the music’s bone structure. Other than that, the gloopy, brightly coloured tones drip like honey as they splay out their tones / arms, floating in life-giving waters. Like a mermaid’s song, sugar-sweet feminine sighs and vocals emanate from within. Sometimes in the ascendency, as if rising up on the tip of a bubble, and sometimes drooping like a shipwreck, Samson’s music is the sound of ambient freedom. Things are better down where it’s wetter. Release date: 18.05.18. www.dauw.bandcamp.com
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑灵感源自创作者在漂浮舱中的深度放松体验，以磁带录音为介质，构建出二十二分钟的器乐音景。弦乐在缓慢呼吸的音层中蜿蜒起伏，节拍仅偶尔出现以维系结构骨架，整体呈现出柔软而具有弹性的漂浮感。人声如美人鱼的歌唱般从深处浮现，时而上升如气泡，时而低垂如沉船。小提琴演奏者与多位环境音乐领域音乐人合作，使专辑在亲密与疏离之间游走。作品探索的是一种在封闭空间中获得的虚假自由——感官被放大，世界被调出频段，却因此更接近极乐。属于独立小厂牌发行的磁带录音环境作品，融合了实验氛围与器乐即兴的边界探索。

items.body:
After the OĽUN album I reviewed enthusiastically a while back, here’s the next project, again motivated and led by violinist/fiddler/composer Ján Kružliak Jr., continuing the rapprochement, indeed embrace, between Slovakia’s traditional music and its classical music. This time it reconnects the works of classical composers who were inspired by and drew on village musics with those traditional sources and styles.
Three ensembles are involved: the Spectrum Quartett led by Kru�liak with two violins, viola and cello; Nogaband, the traditional-style quartet of fiddles, contra (chording viola) and bass that’s led by fiddler and singer Michal Noga; and the female vocal group Ulijanky, plus guest singer Simona Hulejov�.
The majority of the tracks are interpretations of works by Slovak composer Eugen Suchon (1908-1993), with others from fellow-Slovaks Ilja Zeljenka (1932-2007) and Alexander Moyzes (1906-1984), and Hungarian B�la Bart�k (1881-1945) who did a lot of his very detailed collecting of folk music in Slovakia.
In each case the sources - musicians and locations in villages across Slovakia - are credited in the notes, and these arrangements and performances reconnect with the energy and traditional vocal sound of those sources.
In no way is this an orchestra-smoothed thing; this is gutsy, brilliantly played and sung music with all the spirit, skill and technique of traditional music, from players and singers who deeply understand and inhabit it. It’s a glorious piece of work, music to luxuriate in. There’s too much richness to begin to detail, but here’s a dip into a few moments to give the flavor. The tracks all have very long titles detailing their sources, so for brevity’s sake I’ll just give track numbers.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由小提琴家兼作曲家小扬·克鲁兹利亚克二世主导，汇聚了三个乐团：弦乐四重奏Spectrum Quartett、传统弦乐四重奏Nogaband以及女声组合Ulijanky，曲目主要改编自斯洛伐克作曲家苏雄、泽伦卡、莫伊泽斯以及匈牙利作曲家巴托克的作品，这些古典作曲家都曾从斯洛伐克乡村音乐中汲取灵感。专辑的独特之处在于重新追溯这些作品的民间音乐源头，将古典改编与原始乡村录音中的能量和声乐传统直接对接。演奏充满力度与技巧，不是管弦乐式的平滑处理，而是扎根于传统音乐精神的鲜活表达，演奏者和歌手对民间音乐有着深入的理解和浸润感。专辑配有详尽的录音来源注释，标注了斯洛伐克各地村庄的音乐人和采集地，展现了古典与民间传统之间的持续对话。

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑聚焦乌克兰被俄罗斯强制迁移的两万名儿童这一沉重主题，将传统民歌与原创作品交织。音乐主要由弓弦乐器、班杜拉琴与钢琴构成，辅以双陶笛独奏，人声时而温柔、时而凌厉。歌词取材于一首关于少女被送往异乡做工的古老歌谣，可被解读为对当代被掠儿童的隐喻；另一首关于自然精灵Rusalka的仪式歌曲则转向粗犷与激烈。加拿大与乌克兰两地音乐家共同参与，其中一位来自马里乌波尔的少女曾是当年被拐儿童之一。整张专辑以女性声乐为核心，跨越国界记录战争的创伤与文化的韧性。

items.body: After the extra-terrestial explorations of Eventyrferd , the previous album from Norway's Camilla Hole Trio, in which sci-fi synth sounds were married with traditional material, their latest release Langs is rather more earthbound. But the quest to look beyond their own country's folk music continues. Camilla Hole's main instrument being the soprano sax, the influence of jazz is unsurprising and this is evident in the opening track �Springleik,� signifying a tune used to accompany the springleik dance from the west of Norway. Initially Hole takes the melody with Egil Kalman and Knut Kvifte Nesheim providing rhythmic support on double bass and drums respectively, with the overdubbing of Kalman's modular synth and Nesheim's vibraphone adding colour. But characteristically for this trio, in which assigned roles are never clearly defined or adhered to, things soon start to move around, with Kalman taking up the melody on his bass, playing the melody in unison with Hole, while Nesheim opens things out further rhythmically. As the whole piece takes on a much more improvisatory feel, Hole plays the melody one more time as things draw to a close. Langs by Camilla Hole Trio
items.label: Taragot
items._cn_summary: 挪威Camilla Hole Trio的专辑《Langs》在延续前作科幻合成器与传统素材融合路径的基础上，将重心回归地面。高音萨克斯主导旋律线，与低音提琴和鼓的节奏支撑形成对话，同时叠加模块合成器与颤音铁琴的音色层次。乐评以开篇曲《Springleik》为例，详述其对挪威西部民间舞曲素材的解构：成员角色不断流动，乐器间旋律互换，即兴段落逐步展开，演奏边界模糊。这种将北欧民谣、爵士即兴与电子音色交织的手法，展现了三重奏对传统形式的拆解与重塑能力。整体专辑体现了斯堪的纳维亚实验爵士在民俗根源与现代声音美学之间持续探索的脉络。

items._cn_summary: The Drin 来自美国俄亥俄州，这张专辑被描述为他们迄今最具野心的作品，将哥特美式民谣、dub、艺术摇滚等多种元素熔于一炉。这种杂糅式的手法本身就具备实验色彩，乐队不满足于单一类型的框架，而是尝试在多个传统之间寻找张力与对话。作为俄亥俄的朋克场景出身，他们将朋克的态度带入更复杂的音响结构中。文章将其定位为'gothic Americana'，暗示了阴暗叙事与美国根源音乐的交汇，同时融入dub的混响空间感和art rock的构局意识。信息来源为Bandcamp Daily，属于独立地下厂牌的传播渠道，但原文仅为简短导语，信息量不足，无法深入判断其具体声音设计的独创程度。综合来看，跨类型融合是亮点，但受限于内容过短，难以给到更高分。

items.album: Ms Xxan releases spoken word dark ambient album ‘Make Yourself the Lie’

items.body: Ms Xxan released the nine-track album “Make Yourself the Lie” on September 8, 2026, via VuMantra Records, available as a free, name-your-price download on Bandcamp. Ms Xxan performs the album’s spoken word poetry herself, processing her voice through synthesized effects and building the backing from dark ambient and noise-industrial soundscapes, with every credit on the record, from writing through final mix, going to her alone. The album carries a content warning for strong and explicit lyrics; depression under present-day conditions runs through its themes, and the nine tracks grow steadily heavier as the sequence progresses: “make yourself the lie.”, “psychic break.”, “doctrine of harm.”, “dissociative parallels.”, “crossing over.”, “discontinuance.”, “disremember.”, “anhedonia.” and “hatchling.” The same material is also published in episode form as the “Ms Xxan” podcast, available on Apple Podcasts and Audiomack, and streams on SoundCloud alongside the Bandcamp release. Make Yourself the Lie by Ms Xxan About Ms Xxan Ms Xxan writes and produces spoken word and industrial noise music from her current base in the Pacific Northwest, a home she plans to leave before long. “Make Yourself the Lie”, released September 8, 2026, is her album for VuMantra Records, a Berlin-based label founded by Vū (Vince Gagliardi) in 2019, who also records as The Nent and LAGÁN. VuMantra describes its output as “endarkening rhythms for dystopic sub-cultures”, with a catalog built on percussive, ritualistic and tribalistic electronic music. “Make Yourself the Lie” was written, performed, composed, produced and mixed entirely by Ms Xxan, and stands as her first release documented on the label alongside the parallel “Ms Xxan” podcast series carrying the same material.

items._cn_summary: Ms Xxan 的首张专辑《Make Yourself the Lie》是一张九曲作品，由她独立完成词作、表演、作曲、制作与缩混全流程。她本人朗诵诗歌，声音经过合成效果处理，背景由暗氛围与噪音工业音景构建。专辑附有强烈与露骨歌词的内容警告，抑郁情绪贯穿整体主题，九首曲目在序列推进中逐步加重，从开场曲直至终曲呈现出层层递进的沉重感。同名播客将同样内容以剧集形式发布，并在多个流媒体平台同步上线。唱片由柏林独立厂牌 VuMantra Records 发行，以自由定价形式在 Bandcamp 提供下载。VuMantra 厂牌以带有仪式感与部落感的打击电子音乐为定位。整体呈现为一位单人艺术家在暗氛围与工业噪音框架内对口语诗的实验探索。

items.body: Italian musician Ystrith released the seven-track dark ambient debut album “The M Rites” on 2 September 2026, self-issued on Bandcamp and also available on Spotify. Across its seven tracks, Ystrith works with Mithraic mystery-cult imagery, the Roman-era worship of the god Mithras, pulling on details like its buried temples and the weathered carvings its followers left behind. The M Rites by Ystrith Ystrith described the album to Side-Line as concerned not only with the surviving relics of the Mithraic cult, but with “the unbridgeable distance between the surviving objects of the cult and the experiences that have been lost with time.” The seven tracks – “Cautes”, “Fading Gates (of Cosmic Enlightenment)”, “Marble Tauroctonies”, “Myth of the Petrogenesis”, “Voces Magicae”, “Solstice at the Spelaeum” and “Cautopates” – take their titles directly from Mithraic iconography and ritual: Cautes and Cautopates are the torch-bearing twin attendants of Mithras in Roman relief carvings, while “tauroctonies” refers to the bull-slaying scene at the centre of Mithraic imagery. Ystrith has described the record’s musical language as moving through “slow metamorphoses, obsessive repetition and dark, suspended atmospheres,” sustained across the album’s running time to match its ritual subject matter. About Ystrith Ystrith is an Italian musician who records ambient and dark ambient music. “The M Rites”, released 2 September 2026, is the project’s debut album, presented as a sustained meditation on the Mithraic mysteries rather than a single-themed track or EP. The release is available to stream on Bandcamp and Spotify.
items._cn_summary: 意大利音乐人Ystrith的首张专辑以古罗马密特拉教仪轨为题材，七首曲目名称直接取自密特拉图像学——火炬双童Cautes与Cautopates、公牛献祭场景tauroctonies、石窟中至日庆典等。作品在概念层面将声音视为考古学实践，试图弥合密特拉崇拜遗存实物与其原始体验之间的不可逾越的时间鸿沟。音乐语言被描述为缓慢的形态演变、执拗的重复与幽暗悬浮的氛围，七轨贯通以呼应仪式主题。整体呈现为一场对古老神秘仪轨的持续冥想，而非松散的单曲集合。这是一张将古代宗教意象与暗氛围结构结合的概念专辑，适合对仪式音乐与考古式声音探索感兴趣的听众。

items.body: More than twenty years after Agonoize emerged from Berlin, there is very little ambiguity left about what the name represents. The band built its identity around severe electronic rhythm, distorted vocals, confrontation and a live language that made physical excess part of the music rather than decoration around it. Their own terminology, Hellektro, became closely associated with the harder end of dark electro and aggrotech, combining EBM, industrial and dark-electronic structures with an unusually direct lyrical vocabulary. Agonoize themselves have never seemed especially interested in respecting the borders of those labels. That history also explains why a short conversation with Chris L in 2026 becomes more interesting than a routine tour update. The existing catalogue carries considerable weight, the visual mythology of the band is instantly recognisable, and songs written years ago remain embedded in club culture. But Chris is not speaking about preservation. After a serious illness interrupted both his physical momentum and his songwriting, he is working on new Agonoize material again, while approaching the band with a strikingly uncomplicated principle: he still makes music because he wants to. Ahead of Agonoize’s 25 September appearance at Klub Łącznik in Wrocław, where they play alongside System Noire and Antibody, I caught up with Chris L about returning to songwriting, refusing genre boxes, anger as creative material, performing after illness and why getting older has done very little to make Agonoize more polite. The Wrocław event features full sets from Agonoize and System Noire, with Antibody as special guest and an Angst Factor aftershow with DJane Nox Occultae and DJ Bjørn. Chris L on Agonoize in 2026 Karo: Agonoize have existed for more than two decades now. What does the band need to mean to you personally in 2026 for it still to be worth continuing? Chris: Why shouldn’t it be worth it? I make music because I love it. That’s really the most important reason. As long as I still have something to say and the passion to do it, it will always be worth continuing. Karo: “Revelation Six Six Sick” is already five years old. Are you actively working towards a new Agonoize chapter, and if so, what has changed in the way you want the band to sound? Chris: Five years ago, I was knocked off my feet by a serious illness. It took a long time to find the strength and inspiration to write new songs again. Now I’m working on new material. Time will tell… Karo: “Adios, Goodbye!” with Antibody was one of the more recent glimpses of your writing outside the existing Agonoize catalogue, and now you are sharing the stage in Poland. Did that collaboration open any ideas you would actually like to take further? Chris: “Adios, Goodbye” is not a musical composition by Agonoize. It’s simply a lyric I wrote. The finished song then sat unused for more than a year, for whatever reason. Jan from Antibody is a permanent part of Agonoize, but this song has nothing to do with the Agonoize album that is currently in the works. Karo: Aggrotech has gone through periods of enormous visibility and others when people almost seemed embarrassed by the term. Do you still identify strongly with that scene, or has Agonoize outgrown the usefulness of the label? Chris: I’ve never tried to put a specific musical label on Agonoize. Agonoize is Agonoize. We make our music the way it feels right to us, and I’ve never been interested in putting the band into a box. Karo: I first saw you at WGT many years ago, when there was literally a warning that “there will be blood on the dancefloor.” Back then, the provocation felt genuinely confrontational. Has your own relationship with shock and theatrical violence changed as both you and the audience have grown older? Chris: Agonoize has always been known for addressing subjects that other people don’t dare to talk about. I’m loud, I’m uncomfortable, and I think that’s a good thing. Being different has always been important to me. I don’t have to please everyone. I am who I am. And that has nothing to do with age either. Our fans range from 8 to 70 years old. Music doesn’t have an age limit. Karo: A show with such a recognisable visual language can eventually become something audiences expect rather than something that unsettles them. How do you stop an Agonoize concert from turning into a ritual recreation of its own mythology? Chris: The lyrics I write speak a very clear language and create a very clear picture. I don’t want to hide things behind unnecessary metaphors or sugarcoat them. If I have something to say, I say it directly. Karo: Your lyrics have always used anger very directly. What genuinely makes Chris L angry enough to write about in 2026, and has that anger become more focused with age, or less? Chris: Just look at the world around you. Everything that is happening out there becomes part of the stories we write. We live in a terrible world, and in many ways it seems to be getting worse rather than better. There is just as much anger, frustration and darkness in the world as there has ever been. Of course, all of that finds its way into my lyrics and, ultimately, into my music. Karo: You played M’era Luna again this summer and will soon move into a much more immediate club setting in Wrocław. Does the scale of the room actually change the way you perform, or is Agonoize supposed to overwhelm the space regardless of its size? Chris: I’ve always preferred playing small clubs. There’s something special about being close to the audience, with no barriers and no distance between us. That direct connection is what I love about live shows. And ultimately, it doesn’t depend on the size of the venue. We perform in front of 10,000 people with the same intensity as we do in front of 150. Karo: Agonoize have a catalogue full of songs audiences expect to hear. When constructing a set now, how do you balance that collective memory against your own need not to spend the evening reproducing the past? Chris: Every show is different. The combination of old and new songs is important, and that mixture should be something people can feel at every show. In the past, two-and-a-half to four-and-a-half-hour shows were not unusual for me. Because of my illness, that’s unfortunately no longer possible. But a shorter show can still be just as intense and uncompromising. Karo: Looking ahead, what do you want the next phase of Agonoize to prove, not to people who already know exactly what “Bis das Blut gefriert” means to them, but to somebody encountering the band for the first time now? Chris: I have nothing to prove to anyone except myself. I just want to be able to do what I’ve always been best at: making music. Ultimately, that’s all I want. About Agonoize Formed in Berlin in 2002, Agonoize became one of the most recognisable names in the harder European electro scene. Their official biography describes the project through a collision of industrial, EBM and dark electro, while the band has long used the term Hellektro for its own particularly abrasive variant of that language. From the early “Paranoid Destruction” period through records and releases such as “Assimilation”, “Blutgruppe Jesus”, “Bis das Blut gefriert” and the later “Revelation Six Six Sick”, aggression has remained central, but so has Chris L’s insistence on direct language and subjects designed to create discomfort rather than polite distance. Side-Line previously spoke with the band in 2020 for the ‘Click Interview’ with Agonoize. The theatrical violence of the concerts, including the band’s notorious “Blutshow”, became part of that identity, but the interview above suggests something more useful about Agonoize in 2026: beneath all the blood, noise and provocation, the continuation of the band still depends on something remarkably basic, Chris L wanting to write music again. Agonoize live, upcoming dates The band’s site marks the Wrocław and Bärenstein dates specifically as Blutshows. 25 September 2026 – Klub Łącznik, Wrocław, Poland (with System Noire and Antibody, doors 19:00, Angst Factor aftershow with DJane Nox Occultae and DJ Bjørn) – Blutshow 24 October 2026 – Dark Dance Treffen, Mannheim, Germany 11 December 2026 – Unholy X-Mas, Bärenstein, Germany – Blutshow 12 December 2026 – Unholy X-Mas, Bärenstein, Germany – Blutshow 25 December 2026 – Dark Storm, Chemnitz, Germany 9 January 2027 – Fabrik, Bruchsal, Germany 6 February 2027 – From Hell, Erfurt, Germany 16-18 April 2027 – Dark Malta, Malta 16 October 2027 – ORWOhaus, Berlin, Germany

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — The most atypical album of David Byrne's career is also his darkest, a record where he returned to experimentation, not with world music or electronica as he had at other times, but with rock in a way he hadn't since the early days of Talking Heads. It was 1994, the era of indie and alternative rock; much had changed since 1992, the year of his previous studio album. That shift may well have influenced the group of musicians he assembled, a lineup that was anything but accidental, featuring Arto Lindsay on guitar (previously with the Lounge Lizards, John Zorn, and Marc Ribot), John Medeski on organ, Bill Ware on vibraphone (formerly of The Jazz Passengers and Groove Collective), and Bebel Gilberto, the daughter of Jo�o Gilberto."A Long Time Ago" begins to unfurl a descending, subtle mist amidst soft layers of guitar, synthesizers, and percussion, while the vocals, initially a mere whisper with a dreamlike, psychedelic quality, gradually begin to reveal their full power. Then, a sonic explosion, driven by distorted guitars and a prominent bassline, sweeps through everything in "Angels." Lyrics full of defiance and poetry, philosophical, too, delivered with deep emotion and vocal power; that vocal timbre also always held a touch of Adrian Belew, at least in its more melodic sense. And when he hit those high notes, leaving just the strumming guitar, accompanied by the bass and his voice declaring he was ready, it was a magnificent moment. It opened up from within like an explosion of light, unlike anything seen before in his career, quite the paradox for his darkest album."Crash" bursts in with a syncopated rhythm, like shattering glass; it is one of those albums where each track is sonically conceived in relation to the one preceding it, adding extra value. A dissonant guitar, paired with unconventional drumming, lends a unique touch, evoking a walk through ruins. It is as if the Smashing Pumpkins and Soundgarden were attempting a funk sound; that is how unusual the blend is, yet it succeeds brilliantly, driven by that deliberately fractured rhythm... all held together by the glue of the vocals."A Self-Made Man" has a hypnotic rhythm and a melody that gradually reveals itself to be magical and spellbinding, as he sings: "Well, I'll trade you my potential, mental illness for your bad teeth. And now we have a black market. A black market for designer genes. They've taken everything from you: the way you walk, the way you smile, the sound of your voice. I don't even know who you are. Who are you now? I am a self-made man (I have nothing left to give) I am a self-made man (I have nothing left to lose)"That is how groundbreaking this album was, and not just musically; although I like several of his solo albums, this one holds a very special place."Back In The Box" sounds modern; the guitars, featuring Arto Lindsay on the more experimental side and David Byrne on the funk side, combined with the bass and the melody in David's phrasing, create a sort of deconstructed Krautrock, albeit heavily distorted, as is the case across most of the album. The familiar Latin rhythms take on a mysterious air here, as evidenced by "Sad Song", while the energy never flags; John Medeski contributes a "gritted-teeth" rhythmic intensity that maintains its drive regardless of genre shifts."Nothing At All" reveals more of Byrne's true essence: he lays his voice bare, stretching notes to their limit amidst dissonant guitar rhythms and a sense of mystery that offers no clues as to his intentions. Only at the very end does he begin to unravel the harmonic thread, a move clearly planned from the start, concluding with instrumental codas driven by heavy cymbal work alongside distorted guitar and organ."My Love Is You" opens with bossa nova-style acoustic guitar notes, then shifts into a stark contrast to what came before, courtesy of Bill Ware. "Lilies Of The Valley" returns to playful, experimental rhythms, driven by a powerful bass and drum foundation, packed with Groove, that builds in intensity while the funk guitar seems to lock in perfectly with David. The finale is a marvelous duet between Todd Turkisher's drums and Bill Ware's vibraphone."You & Eye" keeps the syncopated funk going, with David playing the clavinet, and features a very delicate chorus that contrasts with the melody's frenetic rhythm. He hadn't lost that knack for composing songs that strike a direct chord, quite the opposite; here, there are echoes of African music in the style of Salif Keita. With Dolette McDonald on backing vocals, the same one who had worked with Sting, Stevie Winwood, and many others."Strange Ritual" is one of the key tracks, where that opening mist returns, dark and dangerous, like Naked City, while the lyrics go: "A man sits in a field, contemplating his crops. Scenes that disgust me, I see myself, I felt awe, I felt disgust, I felt bliss, I felt lust, It is not unusual, I saw people in a remote village, proudly sporting their digital watches. I saw a young Indonesian woman, possessed by the spirit of the Ninja Turtles. I saw palatial mansions with decaying decor and human furniture. I saw a legislature of women being courted by corporate lobbyists. A town whose own inhabitants do not even remember its name. We have a strange ritual. We keep it to ourselves. We are lost in love"There is a restrained violence, and gradually, in the vein of King Crimson's "Indiscipline", a section marked by calm and camouflaged rage, by a lurking violence, erupts; the vocals shift in tandem with the intensity of the music and the musicality of the words. From the mist emerges a nightmare where playing the lead role isn't frightening, because we are in control. We will never hear a more rock-oriented, fully committed David Byrne; it brings to mind King Crimson's improvisations on Starless and Bible Black. It is almost on that level."Buck Naked" is essentially just the guitar, John Medeski's organ, and David's vocals, with him giving it his all, whether in moments of presence or absence. It plays with the contrasts between calm and rage seen in his Psycho Killer era. Yet there is no nostalgia here; he breaks away from the past to launch a new phase, unafraid to keep experimenting and embracing new influences, much as he would later do with the Balanescu Quartet on 1997's Feelings. However, nowhere else is there such a sincere, honest, and unadorned outpouring of the heart as on this album, which, like the other side of a mirror, features his surname spelled in reverse.
items._genre: art rock / experimental rock / avant-pop / funk
items._cn_summary: 这张1994年的专辑是David Byrne职业生涯中最非典型也是最黑暗的一张。他回归摇滚实验路线，组建了一支极具个性的阵容：Arto Lindsay的实验吉他、John Medeski的风琴、Bill Ware的颤音琴以及Bebel Gilberto参与。专辑中歌曲彼此关联，音轨之间形成有机衔接。从开篇的低语式迷幻氛围，到爆炸性的失真吉他冲击，再到切分节奏营造的废墟感，Byrne将funk的律动与avant-rock的不协和张力融合在一起。歌词充满哲学意味与社会批判，探讨身份、基因市场与人性异化等主题。整体制作介于主流另类摇滚的框架与真正的先锋实验之间，是一次成功的跨界探索，但实验深度未完全触及地下前沿领域。

items.body: Review by alainPP — Uncompromising art rock for a fresh sound, minimalist and captivating alternative electro-prog."My Blistering Mind" boasts a distinctive sound, phrased vocals, and electronic, synth-heavy orchestration reminiscent of Porcupine Tree. A final mantra-like repetition of the gentle chorus shifts between pop, cold wave, and Bowie-esque dance-pop-rock, all set to poignant lyrics about mental fragility. "The Mandatory Prize" features a synthetic riff on electric piano, a long, melancholic, and pervasive melody set to lyrics by Dick, with a sound reminiscent of Steve Wilson. Malcolm's voice is ever-present, pale, cold, and robotic, mirroring the synth pads in a new prog style. But that riff is truly gut-wrenching. "Never Really Felt Like Home," with its ambient, hypnotic, and contemplative intro, and Kathryn's deep flute, is a symbol of tranquility. The piccolo allows for a drift into a cinematic-melancholic space where the low guitar solo amplifies this beatific, solemn instrumental. "Smile, Smile, Smile," already seen on the EP, has a haunting metronomic sound on the vibrating bass, the keyboard unfolding, flirting with Esth�sie, the addictive vocals leading to saturation. An electronic Wilson, like his side project No-Man. A stressful, redundant finale leading to musical madness through its endless repetition, the lyrics cruelly explaining this moment of schizoid disarray. "Intermission," as its name suggests, is an instrumental on bass and drums with a jazzy piano, a way of dreaming about the evolution of jazz today. The ensuing Mellotron chills the ears before the colorful piano nods to the works of Joe Jackson."Parallel Lives," with its hushed vocals and contemplative ballad-like feel, sees Kathryn's guitar work on the chorus amplify its solemnity. The effective rhythmic foundation drives this lament, reminiscent of Springsteen's "Streets of Philadelphia." The eponymous track plunges into the depths of Wavy's pop. "Eversion," one of the longer pieces, meanders with lyrics reminiscent of Kate Bush, its orchestration blending neoclassical, synth, and electronic elements, inspired by Steve Wilson. A piano and synth interlude precedes the electric return and Malcolm's vocals, sly, dark, and haughty. The guitar solo brightens the ear, and the sound returns with hypnotic, syncopated percussion, amplifying the progressive, schizophrenic feel. "Pretty Blue Fox" opens with a modern, electro-synth feel, reminiscent of Tangerine Dream in the 70s. It's a blend of electro and prog, with a satisfying mid-section, scraping away at the repetitive sounds of Philip Glass for a restrained, immersive, orgasmic finale ? pure bliss. "Just Another Thing" returns to new prog rock with its piercing, guttural vocals; you'll want to try these breathless vocalizations yourself. There's a hint of Bowie, a sound reminiscent of Simple Minds, a dynamic track with a neo-Marillion-esque keyboard solo, recounting Malcolm's retinal mishaps. "Dropping The Mask" is another instrumental with an electrified, upbeat tempo and bouncy keyboard, a nod to Tangerine Dream in the 80s ? groovy, energetic, and catchy. "Just Hold On (Pts 1 & 2)" opens with a religious, elegiac intro, the soaring choir drifting into hyperspace?a fitting way to escape this groundbreaking album. A striking mix of languid atmosphere and archaic feel, thanks to a guitar emerging from a cloud of Olympus, the solo spreading to the heavens. Malcolm finally appears on this melting synth, the drums merely controlling the rhythm. A solemn ambiance is created by the double bass, the deep vocals, the ephemeral piano, and the final, melancholic guitar outro, a meditative and hopeful finale. A truly beautiful and contemplative ending. "My Blistering Mind," in a shorter, perhaps faster version, and "The Mandatory Prize" are released as radio edits, destined for the airwaves of a better world.HATS OFF GENTLEMEN IT'S ADEQUATE blends vocal and purely instrumental tracks, delivering electronic art-rock with contemporary classical touches. A modern progressive rock sound for the new millennium. (4.5)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑定位为Crossover Prog，以合成器为主导构建电子化前卫摇滚骨架，融合艺术摇滚的冷峻质感与人声实验。主唱Malcolm的演唱风格苍白、机械化，贴近合成器垫底的音色调性，呈现出Porcupine Tree、Steven Wilson及No-Man一脉的英式电子前卫脉络。多首作品采用极简重复的冥想式结构，如念咒般循环副歌，配合精神脆弱主题的歌词，形成催眠式的内省氛围。器乐编排涵盖电钢琴合成riff、低保真长笛独奏、Mellotron冷音色以及新古典倾向的合成器织体，部分段落向Tangerine Dream、Philip Glass的极简重复美学靠拢。爵士化间奏与Joe Jackson式的色彩钢琴点缀其间，为整体阴郁氛围增添呼吸感。整体制作在冷浪潮、舞曲流行与前卫摇滚之间游走，合成器音色层次丰富但仍属类型框架内的稳健探索。

items.body: Bristol project Allflaws released the album The Age Of Nefarious on September 21, 2026, through UK independent label Derelict State Records. The album runs 14 tracks over one hour and one minute, and is available to buy on iTunes and Amazon. Allflaws is the work of Gabriel Curran, who mixes industrial hip hop, trip hop, breakbeat, electronica and dark electronic music on “The Age Of Nefarious”. The album keeps heavy beats, distorted textures and atmospheric production under raw rap vocals, its atmosphere stays tied to Bristol trip hop, but the record leans harder into industrial hip hop’s heavier low end and lets experimental electronica break the production into fractured, glitching textures. Derelict State Records describes the album’s lyrics as exploring control, conformity, digital identity, cultures of violence, low-trust societies, and human resilience. Allflaws’ ‘The Age Of Nefarious’ pushes past the Bristol trip hop sound Derelict State Records, the independent UK label operating out of Bristol and London, works across trip hop, electronica, dub, breakbeat and the darker end of industrial music, including industrial hip hop, industrial electro and EBM. “The Age Of Nefarious” is distributed by Catapult, the same distributor behind Allflaws’ catalog since its earliest releases. An album trailer for “The Age Of Nefarious” is also online on YouTube. Side-Line previously covered Allflaws’ recent standalone singles, including “Vanity Matrix” in 2025, “Chimera” in 2024, and “Antifragile” in 2023. About Allflaws Allflaws was established in Bristol in 2004 by Gabriel Curran, who remains its only official member, writing, producing and performing every release. Curran’s vocal style combines rapping and singing with dark, poetic lyrics, and the project has built its sound around industrial, trip hop and breakbeat elements since its start. Allflaws signed to Catapult and Derelict State Records and released the album “These Walls Are Lies” in 2007, followed by the EPs “Ghost Of The System” and “Replicant Breed” and the album “Black Box Here After” in 2009. The singles “Escaping Sanity” (2010), “Amrak” (2011) and “Interfearence” (2011) preceded the “R Complex” EP and the single “Manufactured Violence” in 2012, and the album “Versus The Soul” in 2013. The album “Apparitions” followed in 2016, then “Mysterium” in 2019 and “Arcana” in 2021. Allflaws released the EP “Ghostrumentals” and the single “Becoming” in 2022, and the single “Antifragile” in 2024. “The Age Of Nefarious”, released September 21, 2026 on Derelict State Records, is Allflaws’ latest full-length, continuing the project’s industrial hip hop and trip hop direction two decades into Curran’s run with Allflaws.

items._cn_summary: Allflaws 是由 Gabriel Curran 自2004年起独自运作的布里斯托项目，新专辑《The Age Of Nefarious》延续其工业嘻哈与trip hop交融的路线，同时向实验电子倾斜。整张专辑14首曲目逾一小时，以沉重的鼓击、扭曲的质感纹理和氛围化的制作铺设底色，原始的rap人声游走其上。制作上保留了布里斯托trip hop特有的阴沉氛围，却进一步压低工业嘻哈的低频重心，并让实验电子的碎裂、故障质感介入声场结构。歌词层面，厂牌描述其探讨控制、顺从、数字身份、暴力文化、低信任社会与人类韧性等主题。专辑由独立厂牌Derelict State Records发行，经Catapult分销，与该艺术家此前的合作渠道一致。该项目长期横跨trip hop、电子、dub、breakbeat与工业音乐领域。

items.body: Am I capable of writing about music without referencing Eurovision? I guess not, especially if the band in question legitimately competed in a recent edition of my beloved song contest. By charming over 76,000 voters with an atmospheric blend of Nordic folk rock, Gåte won the 62nd Melodi Grand Prix, subsequently leading to their appearance at the Eurovision Song Contest 2024, representing Norway. Despite moving on from their allotted semifinal, the group placed dead last amongst the twenty-five finalists. The chaotic performance of their song "Ulveham" didn't impress international audiences or the professional jury, but it sure as hell made an impact on one American Eurofan, and the consensus among hardcore watchers is that Gåte was brutally robbed. After their undeserved flop, Gåte retreated to the forests of Norway for two years, finally reemerging with Sigil—a grander full-length to rekindle the sylvan aura they condensed and presented to over a hundred million people in just three minutes. I like to think of Gåte like a wreath. The center is vocalist Gunnhild Sundli. Her vocalizations—whether singing or chanting—have an unmistakable inflection that drifts over each piece with both tenderness and command. When she dips down into her lower register, the atmosphere turns foggy, but when Sundli lifts her tones high she effortlessly clears the fog to reveal a lively forest. Her technique is perfect for this genre of folk rock, and probably the main reason for Gåte's longevity as a band. Adorning the surrounding area of the wreath are class-act musicians wielding an assortment of traditional instruments. Right-hand man Magnus Børmark plays guitar but also the Swedish nyckelharpa, drummer Jon Even Schärer handles all sorts of percussion, as well as a mouth harp, and Arent Todal tackles various stringed instruments. Further adding to the wreath (specifically to Sigil) is the legion of session artists. I may not be able to quickly discern Marit Aspås's cello from Olav Luksengård Mjelva's hardanger fiddle, but these instruments are key in creating the record's environment. Don't expect these instruments to shred at full capacity. Sigil is a slow burner, churning atmospheres with crescendos rather than jamming out. Although the ambiances Gåte builds are splendid, not a single song runs over five minutes long. This hinders what these ten songs could be. The best pieces like "Strandvaskar" pull off heavy-hitting, successful climaxes, while others like "Nokon" spend too much time creating the liftoff for a climax. I adore the slow songs, especially the pairing of ballads ending the album, and now that the band is on a bigger label, a more digestible approach to their wizardry is expected. But if Gåte's mission is to conjure grand images of Nordic myths and legends, packing it all into three-minute chunks probably isn't the right way to go about it. Sigil by Gåte
items._genre: Nordic folk rock / world fusion / folk
items._cn_summary: 挪威乐队Gåte在经历Eurovision失利后回归，推出专辑Sigil，以北欧民谣摇滚为核心框架。主唱Gunnhild Sundli的声线兼具低沉雾霭与高亢穿透力，统领整张专辑的氛围走向。乐队成员使用瑞典nyckelharpa键琴、hardanger小提琴、口琴等多种传统乐器，配合大量客座乐手构建层次丰富的森林意象。专辑采用慢热式编曲策略，依靠渐进式渐变营造宏大场景，但部分曲目因时长限制未能充分展开其潜力。整体呈现出对北欧神话与传说的音乐化再现，将传统器乐置于现代摇滚结构之中，是一次对民族音乐遗产的当代诠释。

items.body: 「世界3大ジャズ・フェス」に数えられるスイスのモントルー・ジャズ・フェスティバル（Montreux Jazz Festival）。これまで幅広いジャンルのミュージシャンが熱演を繰り広げてきたこのフェスの特徴は、50年を超える歴史を通じてライブ音源と映像が豊富にストックされている点にある。その中からCD、DVD、デジタル音源などでリリースされている「名盤」を紹介していく。 アブドゥーラ・イブラヒム、あるいはダラー・ブランド。アパルトヘイト下の南アフリカでジャズの演奏を始め、その後国外に逃れて音楽活動を続けた名ピアニストが91年の長い人生を終えたのは、今年(2026年)の6月だった。ソロ、デュオ、トリオ、コンボ、オーケストラと、あらゆるフォーマットで作品を残した彼の音楽のエッセンスに触れられるのが、1980年のモントルー・ジャズ・フェスティバルの記録『アット・モントルー』である。そのアルバムを紹介しながら、彼のキャリアを偲ぶ。 『アフリカン・ピアノ』の衝撃 ダラー・ブランドがイスラム教に改宗し、名をアブドゥーラ・イブラヒムとしたのは1968年である。彼の代表作として知られる『アフリカン・ピアノ』が、デンマークの首都コペンハーゲンでライブ録音されたのは69年だから、その時点で彼はすでにアブドゥーラ・イブラヒムになっていたことになる。しかし彼は、ダラー・ブランドとしてその後しばらく活動を続けた。 『アフリカン・ピアノ』の名義は、現行盤ではアブドゥーラ・イブラヒムとなっているが、長らくダラー・ブランド名義で流通してきた。ダラー・ブランドという名の方が現在でも通りがいいのは、ひとえに『アフリカン・ピアノ』の圧倒的な知名度による。 もっとも、ダラー・ブランドという名も実は本名ではなく、出生名をアドルフ・ヨハネス・ブランドといった。ダラーとは「ドル」のことで、南アフリカの故郷ケープタウンの港に寄港した水兵にドル札を渡してジャズのSP盤を熱心に収集していたことで、ダラーが彼のニックネームとなったのだった。 名作『アフリカン・ピアノ』の原盤権を当初持っていたのは、デンマークで1969年から72年までの短い期間活動したスペクテイター・レコードだった。73年になってECMのサブ・レーベルであるJAPOからリリースされたことで、このアルバムは広く世界に知られることになった。現在では、この作品はECMを代表するピアノ・ソロ作としての地位を不動のものにしている。アブドゥーラ・イブラヒムのほかのアルバムは聴いたことがなくても、『アフリカン・ピアノ』は何度も聴いたというジャズ・ファンはわが国でも少なくないと思う。 70年代初頭と言えば、モダン・ジャズが雑多な要素を吸収して鵺（ぬえ）のような音楽に変貌しつつあった頃だが、その時代でも『アフリカン・ピアノ』は奇異な作品であったと思う。延々と繰り返される反復フレーズ。スコールのように畳みかける旋律。隙間なく連続し、どこが始まりでどこが終わりか判然としない楽曲──。それは、アメリカのジャズ、あるいはアメリカの黒人音楽とは明らかに異質な音楽だった。 南アが生んだ3人の世界的ミュージシャン 現在聴くことができるアブドゥーラ・イブラヒムの最も古い録音は、ジャズ・エピッスルズというセクステットによるもので、レコーディングは1959年であった。このバンドには、やはりのちに世界的なミュージシャンとなるトランペッターのヒュー・マセケラも在籍していた。マセケラが「グレイジング・イン・ザ・グラス」で全米1位を獲得するのは68年のことである。 ジャズ・エピッスルズのメンバーのうち3人は、南ア初の黒人ミュージカル『キング・コング』に参加していて、マセケラもそのひとりだった。『キング・コング』のヒロインとして舞台に立ったのがミリアム・マケバで、彼女もまたのちに世界的シンガーとなる。マセケラとマケバは、わずか2年だが結婚していたこともあった。アブドゥーラ・イブラヒム、ヒュー・マセケラ、ミリアム・マケバ。南アが生んだこの3人のスターが同じコミュニティから出発したのは、南アのジャズ・シーンそのものが小さなコミュニティだったからである。 ジャズ・エピッスルズは、南アで公式に発売された初めての黒人ジャズ・バンドのレコードだった。『ヴァース1』がそのタイトルだったが、『ヴァース2』が録音されることはついになかった。アパルトヘイト下の南アにあって、黒人ならびにその音楽であるジャズに対する弾圧がほどなく激化したことがその理由である。 南ア独自のタウンシップ・ジャズ 1994年まで南アフリカの政権を握ったNP（国民党）が、悪名高い人種分離政策であるアパルトヘイトを掲げたのは1948年だった。南ア人は、「白人」「カラード」「インド人」「アフリカ人」の4つのカテゴリーに分けられ、結婚やセックスによる人種混淆を妨げる法律が整備されて、居住区の分割や都市における人種隔離が進められた。 人種の分類上、ヒュー・マセケラとミリアム・マケバは「アフリカ人」、アブドゥーラ・イブラヒムは白人と黒人の混血である「カラード」であった。3人はいずれも1960年代に母国をあとにしたが、その後マセケラとマケバが90年代まで一度も帰国が叶わなかったのに対し、イブラヒムは何度か国に帰ることを許されている。これは、「アフリカ人」と「カラード」の法的権利の違いによるものだったと思われる。 人種分離は、トイレ、レストラン、ホテル、劇場から、バス、学校、役場にまで及び、社会生活のあらゆる領域が「ヨーロッパ人」向けと「非ヨーロッパ人」向けに分けられた。「ヨーロッパ人」とは、南アへの初期入植者であるオランダ人と、その後入植してきたイギリス人を主に指す。 しかし、オランダ人とイギリス人の間にもまた格差はあって、南アの経済、政治、社会の上層を長らく支配してきたのはイギリス人だった。イギリス人支配に対するオランダ人のルサンチマンの結晶のような政党がNPで、その初期の構成員の多くは、戦時にあってナチス・ドイツを支持した者たちだった。政権を握った彼らが設計したアパルトヘイトの諸制度は、しばしばナチスのユダヤ人政策に比して語られる。 アパルトヘイトは、アメリカ南部で1860年代から100年間にわたって存続した人種差別法「ジム・クロウ法」にも似ていたが、それ以上に残酷であったのは、アメリカにはなかった黒人の強制移住があったことによる。 1923年に施行された原住民都市地域法という法律によって、黒人は「タウンシップ」と呼ばれた隔離居住区に住むことを強制された。最も古いタウンシップはイブラヒムの故郷であったケープタウンにあって、その後南ア全土にタウンシップが設けられた。ここで独自に発展したのが、タウンシップ・ジャズである。 アメリカのラグタイムやスウィングと南アの土着の音楽が混じり合って生まれたのがタウンシップ・ジャズで、そこにカリブ海の音楽の要素も感じられるのは、ニューオリンズを経由してもたらされた影響があったからかもしれない。また、南アはある時期までイギリスの旧植民地や入植地の共同体である英連邦の構成国であったから、同じく英連邦の国であったジャマイカやバルバドスから音楽が伝わるルートもおそらくあっただろう。 禁じられたジャズと音楽家たちの出国 1950年代になって、タウンシップ・ジャズと、その後に輸入されたアメリカのジャズをベースにしたジャズ・バンドがいくつか生まれた。ジャズ・エピッスルズがその代表格だったが、彼らが最初のアルバムをレコーディングしてほどなく、南ア史に残る事件が起きた。1960年3月21日の「シャープヴィル虐殺」である。 アパルトヘイト下の南アでは、黒人に身分証の常時携帯を義務づける「パス法」という法律があった。それに抗議するために南アの首都ヨハネスブルグ近郊シャープヴィルの警察署に集まった黒人群衆に警察が発砲した事件が「シャープヴィル虐殺」で、これによって69人が殺され、180人以上が負傷した。 反アパルトヘイト運動のリーダーであり、1962年に逮捕されて以後27年間を獄中で過ごしたのがネルソン・マンデラだった。アパルトヘイト撤廃後の新生南ア初の大統領に就任した彼の歩みを描いた映画『マンデラ 自由への長い道』に、シャープヴィル虐殺の場面が出てくる。犠牲者の多くは、警察の装甲車から逃げ惑う中、背後から無差別に撃たれたのだった。この事件は海外各国に衝撃を与え、国連は3月21日を国際人種差別撤廃デーと定めた。 この事件をきっかけに、南ア全土に抗議行動が広がり、それにともなって南ア政府の弾圧も激化した。ジャズの演奏やラジオでの放送も禁止され、ジャズ・エピッスルズは解散を余儀なくされた。その後、先の3人は故郷を後にすることになる。ヒュー・マセケラがロンドンに活動の場を移したのが1960年、アブドゥーラ・イブラヒムが欧州に移住したのが62年で、これはマンデラが逮捕されたのと同じ年であった。ミリアム・マケバは、反アパルトヘイト運動に関与した咎で、67年に国外追放されている。 サックス・プレーヤーとしてのイブラヒム 欧州に活動の場を求めたアブドゥーラ・イブラヒムの庇護者となったのが、デューク・エリントンだった。スイスにツアーで訪れていたエリントンにイブラヒムの演奏を聴くよう懇願したのは、彼の婚約者であったと伝わる。 イブラヒムのトリオの演奏を気に入ったエリントンは、この有望なピアニストのワールドワイドのデビュー作となる『デューク・エリントン・プレゼンツ・ザ・ダラー・ブランド・トリオ』のレコーディングを支援した。リリースされたのは、フランク・シナトラが1961年に設立したリプリーズ・レコードからだった。 その後イブラヒムは数々のアルバムをレコーディングすることになるが、最も多くのアルバムを残したのは、ドイツのレーベル、エンヤ（Enja）である。エンヤの設立は1971年で、これはECM設立の翌年に当たる。Enjaというレーベル名は「European New Jazz」の略で、この場合の「New」はアメリカのジャズに対して「新しい」のみならず、ECMよりもさらに「新しい」音楽を目指そうとする意気込みの表現でもあっただろう。 1980年、イブラヒムはモントルー・ジャズ・フェスティバルに出演して8曲を演奏した。うち6曲を収録したライブ盤がリリースされたのも、やはりエンヤからだった。 バンドは、アルト・サックス、トロンボーンをフロントに擁したクインテットだったが、冒頭の「ツァクヴェ」では明らかに3本の管の音が聞こえる。日本盤CDのライナーノーツには「3管を含むセクステットの一体感をアピールしている」という意味不明の記述があるが、3管に聞こえるのはイブラヒムもサックスを吹いているからである。 イブラヒムは、ピアノ以外にフルートやチェロなどを奏する多才な音楽家だった。モントルーではソプラノ・サックスを吹いていて、それがたんなる余技とは言えないのは、6曲中3曲でピアノを弾かずにソプラノを吹いているからだ。裏ジャケットのクレジットも「Soprano Saxophone, Piano」と、サックスが先になっている。 アルバムの最後の曲「イシュマエル」は、ベースの反復フレーズが延々と繰り返されるイブラヒムの代表曲のひとつだが、この曲で彼は堂々たるサックス・ソロを披露していて、吹き終えたのち、客席から大きな喝采を受けている。 イブラヒムの音楽の広大な世界 モントルーのライブ盤はわずか6曲だが、驚くほど多様であったイブラヒムの音楽がこの一枚に凝縮されていると感じる。タウンシップ・ジャズ、サンバ、アラビア音楽、デューク・エリントン、セロニアス・モンク──。これも彼の代表曲である「ザ・ウェディング」は、雑多な原料を混ぜ合わせ、それを蒸留したのちに残った原酒のように澄明で美しい。 アルト・サックスのほかにフルートも吹くカルロス・ワードはパナマ出身のプレーヤーで、ジョン・コルトレーン、ドン・チェリー、セシル・テイラーらとの共演で知られている。イブラヒムとは、ドン・チェリーとのトリオで録音した1972年のライブ盤『第三世界＝アンダーグラウンド／The Third World-Underground』からのつきあいであり、その後デュオ作も一緒にレコーディングしている。 『第三世界＝アンダーグラウンド』は何度も繰り返し聴きたくなる名作である。チェリーの個性が大いに発揮されているが、とくにアヴァンギャルドな作品ではない。このアルバムと、ソロ作の『アフリカン・ピアノ』、さらにオーケストラと共演した何枚かの作品のうちのひとつ、例えば『アフリカ組曲／African Suite』などをこのモントルーのライブ盤と合わせて聴けば、アブドゥーラ・イブラヒムの広大な世界の概要を知ることができると思う。エンヤにレコーディングされたアルバムから10曲をセレクトした『プレミアム・ベスト』というCDもまた、格好の手引きとなるだろう。 2011年のモアーズ・フェスティバルにて 独唱によって閉じられた長いキャリア 2024年、アブドゥーラ・イブラヒムはロンドンのバービカン・センターでコンサートを行い、その演奏をレコーディングした。フルート奏者と、ベース／チェロ奏者とのトリオによるライブで、そのアルバムに『3』というタイトルがつけられたのは、トリオ演奏であるからだけではなく、アルバムが3部構成になっているからである。 1部には、ライブ前の無観客のホールで、8トラックのアナログ・テープ・マシンで録音した6曲が収録されている。資料によれば、この機材はエルヴィス・プレスリーがデビュー曲「イッツ・オール・ライト」を録音した際に使ったものであり、メンフィスのサン・スタジオにあったその機材を現在所有しているのは、ブラーのデーモン・アルバーンだそうである。そのテープ・マシンを、デーモンのスタジオからバービカン・センターに運んで録音が行われたのだった。 2部、3部は客を入れたのちのライブ演奏で、2部ではイブラヒムのヒーローであったエリントンの「イン・ア・センチメンタル・ムード」と、ジョン・コルトレーンの「ジャイアント・ステップス」、3部ではセロニアス・モンクの「スキッピー」を演奏している。 2部と3部には「リプライズ」と題されたピアノ・ソロの演奏が収められているが、注意深く耳を傾ければ、その中にジャズ・エピッスルズの名曲「ブルース・フォー・ヒューイ」のメロディを聴くことができる。「ヒューイ」はヒュー・マセケラの愛称である。南アのジャズの歴史をともにつくった古い友に対する変わらぬ友情をイブラヒムは示そうとしたのかもしれない。マセケラの死去から6年が経っていた。 2回目のアンコールで、イブラヒムはアカペラで歌を歌っている。アフリカの民族語と英語をまじえて歌われるその歌には、「伝達──幾世紀の歴史をもつ海運貨物の音」というタイトルがつけられている。何世紀にもわたって海運で運ばれていった貨物。それが何を意味するか、言うまでもあるまい。 このアルバムが、結果的にアブドゥーラ・イブラヒムの遺作となった。アフリカの奴隷貿易の歴史を歌う独唱で、イブラヒムは長いキャリアを閉じた。彼の新作がもはや聴けなくなった今、残された膨大な作品の森にあらためて分け入りたく思う。 文／二階堂 尚 『At Montreux』 アブドゥーラ・イブラヒム／ダラー・ブランド ■1.Tsakve 2. Whoza Mtwana 3. The Homecoming Song 4. The Wedding 5. The Perfumed Forest Wet With Rain 6. Ismael ■アブドゥーラ・イブラヒム(ss,p)、カルロス・ワード(as,fl)、クレイグ・ハリス(tb)、アロンゾ・ガードナー(b)、アンドレ・ストロパート(ds) ■第14回モントルー・ジャズ・フェスティバル／1980年7月18日   投稿 【アブドゥーラ・イブラヒム】長い歩みを終えた南アフリカの名ピアニスト ─ライブ盤で聴くモントルー Vol.69 は ARBAN に最初に表示されました。

items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评以1980年蒙特勒爵士音乐节现场录音为切入点，回顾南非钢琴家阿卜杜拉·伊布拉欣的传奇生涯。文章追溯他从开普敦出发、与休·马塞拉和米里亚姆·马凯巴共同成长的社区背景，详细梳理阿帕特heid时代下南非黑人音乐家的流散经历，以及'township jazz'这一独特音乐传统的形成脉络。文章着重分析伊布拉欣音乐中反复的乐句、层叠的旋律段落和模糊的曲式结构，指出其与美国黑人音乐的明显差异。作为ECM厂牌旗下代表作品，《非洲钢琴》以简洁的钢琴独奏展现了南非本土音乐语汇与世界爵士语汇的融合，是理解伊布拉欣艺术世界的入口。

items.body:
Though this recording documents the work of thirteen of Belgium's most innovative ensembles, the real star is the Park Abbey located just outside Leuven and founded in 1129. Built and maintained for the purpose of quiet meditation, the abbey hosted the musicians who used the quiet surroundings to prepare and record their unique musical imaginings. The result is a mostly instrumental collection that mines the riches of Belgian folk and world music traditions, including Romani scales,
La Pump
rhythms, and accordion-based
bal-musette
flavors.
For example, Slovenian-native R�n�lius Bikar�s searing violin opens the set with �R�fuge.� He and his self-named ensemble channel pan-European Roma history.
Meanwhile, �Poor Boy� is a Django Reinhardt-inspired swing tune by Charlotte Pelgen & Bipolar Bows. Pelgen sings in English, and with her ukulele strumming sounding very much like a tenor banjo, the tune is enlivened by Lotte Remmen�s St�phane Grappelli-like fiddle lines.
The distinctive sound of the oud announces yet another musical tradition. Blending Mediterranean with Arabic sounds, the Lebanese-Belgian singer Amber Haddad and her trio, oudist Adil Benhsain and double bassist Martijn Vanbuel, spin a beguiling musical web. According to the liner notes (translated from the Dutch), �Tawazden� is about �seeking balance and finding peace within a complex environment.� Further, �the various spaces of the abbey and their murals are the direct source of inspiration.�
The accordion is especially prominent. So too is the Western classical tradition. Sounding almost Baroque, �Sacristia Invisibilis,� is another standout for me. Here, mandolinist Andries Boone is joined by Anouk Sanczuk on octave violin (sometimes called the baritone violin, tuned an octave lower than standard) and on harpsichord Sandra Van der Gucht. They create an indescribable sound you have to hear.
Throughout, the Abbey�s stone presence looms. Aur�lie Charneux�s solo clarinet piece �L'Ape Millenaria� is about a thousand-year-old bee that haunts the abbey. �Thila,� by Enara Navaira, evokes ancient Celts with a jazzy double bass and drum kit behind throat singing and Citera (a kind of Hungarian zither).
Airboxes is a duo who mix chromatic and diatonic accordions. Their offering �Abdij 1� sounds improvised. Again from the liner notes, �they share their impressions of the timelessness of monastic life.�
Despite the wide range of styles,
The Sound of the Abbey
has a coherence, perhaps informed by the artists� shared inspiration. The record is often surprising and always soothing. Three years in the making, the ensembles were lovingly recorded and mixed by Bert Huysentruyt and mastered by Pieter De Wagter from Equus Mastering. They have rendered a warm sound using the natural reverb of ancient stone provided by the project�s silent partner.

items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. items._cn_summary: Alison Cotton 的新专辑延续了她标志性的模糊边界风格，融合民谣、前卫音乐与宗教仪式感。中提琴、簧风琴、击弦古钢琴与钢琴构成主要乐器编制，此作新增鼓、贝斯与合成器，拓展了声音维度。多数曲目为即兴创作并以单次录音完成，营造出穿越时空的静谧神秘氛围。约翰·克莱尔诗作被谱成旋律，叠加持续嗡鸣声底，呈现出超越性美感。专辑中段《Sprigs of Heather》以中世纪圣咏开篇，发展为钢琴主导的缓慢级进旋律，被视为整张作品的珍珠。专辑同时是一份纪念，寄托着对2024年末辞世的父亲的哀思——《The Final Harvest》记录父亲最后一次造访他深爱的菜园，浸透无言的温柔。光明与黑暗在此交织渗透，作品拒绝被简单归类，只以 Alison Cotton 自己的名字作为定义。

items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)
items.label: Analog Africa
items._genre: Benin funk / Afro-Cuban / vodun / Congolese rumba
items._cn_summary: Analog Africa 厂牌将贝宁传奇乐团 Orchestre Poly-Rythmo 与词曲创作者 Antoine Dougbé 1977 至 1982 年间的合作整理成辑。Dougbé 以拍击大腿的 Cavacha 节奏闻名，并因其巫毒信仰背景和严苛的演出要求而被称作「恶魔首相」。专辑收录三张录音室专辑及若干单曲，展现出古巴 son、刚果 rumba 与贝宁本土 vodun 元素交织的色彩。编曲中高帽节奏持续推进，合成器铺垫与塑料质感吉他相互交织，部分曲目更呈现出明显的古巴 son 影响。整体制作保留了七十年代末至八十年代初录音的原始质感，是了解西非流行音乐史中这段跨文化交汇的重要文献。

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

Vanishment
(Review)

Genuine Negro Jig
(Review)
items.label: Buda Musique
items._genre: bal-musette / French chanson / ragtime / jug band / eclectic fusion
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由吉他手兼歌手Dominique Cravic与一群法国乐手共同录制，融合了法国传统bal-musette手风琴音乐、拉格泰姆、jug乐队、法国香颂与skiffle等多种风格，涵盖27首短曲。乐器组合极为多样，包括手风琴、萨克斯、木琴、单簧管、班卓琴、尤克里里、特雷门琴、夏威夷吉他、风笛及音乐锯等，营造出在两间阁楼中翻找出78转唱片并即兴演奏的氛围。Cravic以类似Maurice Chevalier的念白式唱腔演绎旧日曲目，既收录1925年的幽默老歌《Ukulele Lady》，也包含向已故法国抵抗运动歌手Juliette Gréco致敬的严肃作品，并将《Smoke Gets in Your Eyes》《Take Five》《As Time Goes By》等经典重新编排。整体呈现出考古式的好奇心与严肃音乐家的投入感，乐评将其比作同样难以归类的Dan Hicks & His Hot Licks，让被遗忘的音乐风格重新焕发活力。

as part of the
Prism Quartet
's new series of collaborations called
Unlocking Your Inner Composer
. If you have listened to my radio programs, you are probably familiar with the quartet's ground-breaking, genre-blurring music. If not, there's no better introduction than this.

items._cn_summary: 作曲家大卫·祖宾斯基为普林斯姆四重奏创作了这首短篇作品，作为"解锁你的内在作曲家"系列合作项目的一部分。作品于2025年11月在费城自由图书馆首演，邀请了人声表演者乌苏拉·拉克、打击乐手泰肖恩·索雷以及小提琴家卡洛斯·圣地亚哥参与编曲与演出。整首作品时长不到四分钟，从原始粗砺的声音质地走向抒情流畅，随后又折返回起点。评论指出乐手在编排中展现出细腻与能量的平衡。作为一份内容较短的推荐性评论，原文缺乏对音乐技法、声音设计或结构安排的具体分析，信息深度有限。Prism四重奏长期以跨界融合著称，本作品延续了其打破流派界限的方向，将当代作曲与即兴元素并置。
